messages:
alex: Quick handoff — I'm oncall until 22:00 UTC. Leaving a short watchlist of known flaky signals and mitigations.

alex: 1) KV cache eviction alerts (svc: redwood-kv). We've seen spikes in evictions leading to higher tail latency for streaming endpoints. Alert channels have been noisy ~every 10–15m. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache. Short-term: I've temporarily raised the eviction alert threshold (see comment in alert rule) and enabled extra logging in the next deploy. If you see sustained >5% eviction rate for >5m, escalate to eng-runtime.

alex: 2) Metrics pipeline lag (svc: metrics-ingester). Intermittent backpressure causes delayed dashboards and stale SLO signals. Symptoms: "ingester_consumer_lag" spikes and ingestion retries. Temp mitigation: consumer concurrency bumped to +2 on staging and prod; full fix tracked in ENG-3321. Query to watch: ```sum(rate(ingester_consumer_lag[5m])) by (instance)``` — watch for >200.

alex: 3) Dedicated autoscaler flaps on reserved pools. We've observed thrashing when burst capacity kicks in for qps bursts ~> model-serve. If autoscale flaps, manual step-up via console works. If you need to, run `redwoodctl pool scale --id rp-123 --replicas 4` (ops perms). I'm leaving a retry script at /runbooks/scale-fix.sh.

alex: 4) Streaming API tail latency: a few requests returned 500 due to KV lookups timing out during eviction storms. If streaming errors surge, fallback to the lower-capacity model variant by setting header `X-Model-Fallback: variant-b`. See rollout policy: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/stream-fallback.

oncall-bot: Rotation note: alex is oncall (shift ends 22:00 UTC). Reminder ping scheduled at 21:30 UTC.

maria: Thanks — noted. For the kv eviction threshold change, did you leave a link to the alert diff?

alex: Yep, linked in the alert rule comment. Also pushed a small alert-rule patch in infra repo: https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/commit/abc123

jordan: Quick q — autoscaler flap: is that specific to rp-123 or other reserved pools too?

alex: Mostly rp-123 and rp-127. Pattern: pools with mixed long-lived and bursty workloads. We've flagged for policy change (ENG-3350) to separate burstable workloads.

sam: I'll keep an eye on metrics-ingester overnight. If lag >300 I'll increase consumer to +4 and page runtime.

maria: One more FYI: onboarding tests for dedicated pools are flakey. Not blocking, but expect a couple of false positives in smoke tests.

alex: Thanks. If anything looks like a real degradation (errors, SLO breaches), ping #eng-sre and add @pager-duty. Otherwise ack here and I'll do handoff 21:50.

jordan: ack :thumbsup:

sam: ack

maria: ack

alex: handing off at 21:50 UTC. Leaving notes in ops journal: /notes/oncall/1748001234.md — contains exact commands.
